why_this_exists.trigger: the v18 selection run produced required literals that were generic words: template, None, inner, raise, callable, should
why_this_exists.why_that_is_a_defect: the registered required literals are the backbone of the frozen strict track and of the frozen regex; generic words make both nearly automatically satisfiable, so the task would silently stop testing whether the model actually read the code, while every downstream field still looked healthy
why_this_exists.who_caught_it: the runner agent caught it in its own selection output and refused to register those candidates; this rule is the integrator's answer, and registering weak literals would have been a quiet downgrade of the evidence bar, not a criterion change
why_this_exists.calibration_against_v16: every v16 sealed and development literal passes this rule, so the rule does not disqualify the tasks that produced the citable confirmation batch

rule.requirement_1: every required literal must appear verbatim in at least one of the four registered views, and its source view must be recorded
rule.requirement_2: at least two of the at most three required literals must be code anchored
rule.requirement_3: both tokens of the frozen regex, the cause token and the fix token, must themselves be code anchored
rule.requirement_4: no required literal may be a Python keyword or a name in the builtins namespace
rule.requirement_5: the lazy answer negative control must fail: a line built only from the issue identifier, the problem statement's own word tokens and generic Python vocabulary must not satisfy the frozen regex and the literal requirement; if it does, the candidate is rejected

code_anchored_definition.a_defined_name: a name that the views themselves bind, extracted with AST: a function, class, method, assignment target or parameter name inside one of the four views
code_anchored_definition.b_constant_token: a token that appears verbatim in the views and is an all caps constant with at least three characters such as E015, a dotted version such as 3.8.3, or a type or exception name such as NoneType
code_anchored_definition.c_quoted_string: a string constant that appears quoted in the views and is not a member of the declared common word stoplist frozen before selection
code_anchored_definition.note: no length threshold is imposed on a defined name: _cull passes as a defined name while template does not, which is the intended behaviour, because being bound by the code is what separates them

v16_sealed_confirmation.verdict: all three sealed tasks pass requirement 2

v18_rejected_literals.template: not bound by the views, common word
v18_rejected_literals.should: not bound by the views, common word
v18_rejected_literals.verdict: the three candidate contracts failed requirement 2 or 4, which is exactly why the runner agent refused to register them

what_must_change_in_the_candidate_contra.views_stay_as_derived: the four views, their ranges and their hashes are not touched by this rule; only the literal list and the two regex tokens are re-derived
what_must_change_in_the_candidate_contra.re_derive_from_the_views: prefer the names the views themselves define that are closest to the defect the statement describes, and prefer a constant token when the statement carries one, exactly as the v16 contracts did

worked_examples.django__django-16255: the views define convert_exception_to_response, response_for_exception, get_exception_response and handle_uncaught_exception, so code anchored literals exist and the contract should use them instead of inner, raise and callable
worked_examples.django__django-15572: template_changed is bound by the first view and is code anchored; template and None are not, so they must be replaced by names bound in the views
worked_examples.django__django-15569: RegisterLookupMixin and _unregister_lookup are both code anchored and already satisfy the rule; should is not and may stay only as the third non decisive literal or be dropped

does_not_mean: this is not a criterion change: the four strict track conditions, the 160 character bound, the retry budget and the paired statistic are untouched
this is not a relaxation in either direction: the rule makes the registration stricter than the run that produced it, and any candidate that fails it is rejected and never replaced by a weaker one
a requirement failure here may not be resolved by widening to a different candidate order: the frozen available order stays in force

blocker_found_in_the_same_proposal.item: statement_hash_matches_preselection is false for all three candidates
blocker_found_in_the_same_proposal.why_it_matters: the plan requires the problem statement hash to reconcile with the public task table exactly as in v16, and the v16 round already had one double hashing incident on the 15315 artifact; a registration that carries false into the registry would make the source provenance unverifiable
blocker_found_in_the_same_proposal.required_action: diagnose the mismatch before registration: state whether the pool stored a hash of a normalised statement, and either reconcile it with a documented rule or record the mismatch as an open provenance gap; the registration may not silently carry false

cap_note: the pilot cap of 90 keeps a margin of 1.304 over the worst case, which satisfies the frozen rule of at least 1.3 but only just; raise it to 100 for margin at no cost, since the cap is a ceiling and not a budget target
